pricing_model: Tiered by store annual revenue (monthly subscription, billed in USD every 30 days)
starting_price_usd: Free under $250k annual revenue; $69/mo entry paid tier; $199/mo advanced plan (custom/enterprise pricing for larger brands)
free_trial_or_freemium: 14-day free trial; effectively freemium for stores under $250k annual revenue
shopify_install_count: ~14 reviews on the Shopify App Store; tracked on ~7 stores per StoreLeads (small but active user base)
shopify_sync_direction: Primarily one-way: Shopify -> Cogsy for historical sales, products, variants, orders, and inventory; Cogsy generates POs and forecasts (writes back limited inventory / PO data) [uncertain on bi-directional inventory write-back]
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants/SKUs, inventory levels (multi-location), orders/sales history, locations; bundles and subscriptions are recognized for forecasting
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes - supports multi-store and multi-warehouse consolidated views
shopify_pos_support: [uncertain] (Shopify POS sales aggregate via the Shopify connection; no documented dedicated POS workflow)
shopify_variant_option_mapping: SKU/variant-level forecasting and reporting; days-of-supply and target stock levels calculated per SKU per location
shopify_real_time_or_batch: [uncertain] - inventory and sales data sync periodically (batched/scheduled refresh, frequency not publicly documented)
shopify_known_limitations: Small install base on Shopify App Store; no public Built-for-Shopify badge confirmed; limited write-back capability documented (forecasts/POs are core output, not deep Shopify inventory mutations); pricing tier is positioned above casual users so under-$250k brands get a free tier while larger brands jump to $199+/mo
etsy_supported: Third-party / [uncertain] - some listings mention Etsy compatibility, but no dedicated Cogsy + Etsy integration page in vendor docs
amazon_marketplaces: [uncertain] (Amazon Seller Central connection documented; specific marketplace coverage not publicly listed)
amazon_seller_types: FBA and FBM (FBA inventory across multiple fulfillment centers explicitly supported); Vendor Central [uncertain]
amazon_synced_entities: Inventory (by FBA location), sales/orders history for forecasting; no documented listing creation or settlement posting
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: Supports FBA restocking recommendations and tracking inventory across fulfillment centers; helps stay within Amazon restock limits. No documented FBA inbound shipment creation workflow.
amazon_settlement_report_handling: Not applicable - Cogsy is a planning/forecasting tool, not an accounting poster; settlements are not journaled by Cogsy
amazon_known_limitations: Cogsy treats Amazon as a sales/inventory data source for demand planning; it does not manage listings, repricing, shipping labels, or settlement accounting
xero_synced_entities: [uncertain] - Cogsy is a demand planning / PO tool, not a full accounting connector; Xero integration is referenced in third-party comparisons but exact entity coverage (invoices, bills, COGS, inventory adjustments) is not publicly documented by Cogsy
xero_known_limitations: Cogsy is not primarily an accounting integration; Xero connection appears focused on sharing financial context (cash flow) rather than transactional posting
qb_synced_entities: [uncertain] - QuickBooks Online connection exists; specific entities (invoices, bills, COGS journals) not publicly documented
qb_known_limitations: QBO appears to be used for cash-flow context within Cogsy's Funds Planner rather than full transactional accounting sync [uncertain]
other_ecom_channels: Amazon, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Walmart, Magento (referenced); 3PLs ShipBob and ShipHero; Cin7 Omni; Katana. TikTok Shop / Faire / Square / eBay not documented.
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes - bundles are recognized and forecasted (component-level demand attribution); details on full kit BOM decomposition [uncertain]
other_accounting_integrations: No documented integrations with Sage, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks, NetSuite, or Wave
bom_support: No - Cogsy does not provide BOM / manufacturing functionality; it is a forecasting and PO tool for finished goods
bin_location_support: No - location-level (warehouse) granularity only, not bin/aisle
multi_warehouse: Yes - multi-location inventory visibility, per-location forecasts, target stock levels, days of supply per SKU per location
barcoding: No native barcode generation or scanning
purchase_orders: Yes - automated PO drafts based on demand forecasts, bulk product add, milestone tracking (draft -> delivery), multi-shipment POs, edit audit trail, supplier auto-fill, partial receipts [uncertain on full partial-receipt support]
supplier_management: Yes - vendor records with contact info, contracts, preferred-supplier-per-SKU mapping, ability to share 12-month production plan with vendors
ai_demand_forecasting: Yes - core product. AI/ML demand forecasting up to 12 months out; what-if scenarios (best-case, worst-case, most-probable); marketing event calendar adjusts forecasts for promotions; ~92% forecast accuracy claim with 6+ months of data
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes - automated PO drafts and restock recommendations with quantities based on historical and real-time inventory data; replenish alerts sent to inbox
public_api: [uncertain] - no public developer documentation or API portal found
integration_architecture: Native direct integrations with platforms (Shopify, Amazon, ShipBob, ShipHero, Cin7, QuickBooks, Xero); no documented iPaaS dependency
mobile_app: No native mobile app documented; web-based platform
sync_frequency: [uncertain] - documented as periodic/scheduled refresh rather than real-time webhook-driven (specific cadence not publicly stated)
shipping_carrier_integrations: None documented (Cogsy is not a shipping/fulfillment tool); relies on 3PL partners (ShipBob, ShipHero) for fulfillment context
three_pl_integrations: Yes - native integrations with ShipBob and ShipHero documented on vendor site; Cin7 Omni connection for retail ops
notable_customers: Caraway (DTC cookware), Lalo (baby/family DTC), Olipop (DTC beverage); referenced via Cogsy case studies and podcast
last_major_release: Smart Replenishment and Funds Planner features highlighted across 2025; Surge Alert example cited in March 2025 case study [uncertain on exact release dates]
last_funding_event: $6M Seed round in December 2021, led by Accel with participation from Bain Capital Ventures and Automattic (WooCommerce); no publicly announced subsequent rounds
